speaker_role: independent counselor/consultant (Senior Strategist and Regional Team Leader at Crimson Education)
commercial_incentive: Produced by Crimson Education, a paid college-admissions consulting company; ends with a call to contact their advisors
key_insights: Describes the Common App personal statement as up to 650 words with several topic prompts, including an open 'anything' option
Recommends choosing a topic that is personally meaningful, not just broadly interesting, since for some colleges it's the only essay submitted
Emphasizes the essay should demonstrate growth or change over time, framed like character development in a story
Advises against resume-style regurgitation of activities/classes already visible elsewhere in the application
Warns against cliche narrative arcs (e.g., the last-second sports-victory story) since admissions officers read thousands of essays and want something unique
Recommends avoiding overly complex vocabulary/sentences and instead reading the essay aloud to check it sounds like the student's natural voice
Describes Crimson's process of submitting multiple topic proposals and having a strategist help select the one that best fits the student's overall application theme
specific_numbers_or_facts: Common App personal statement word limit stated as up to 650 words
notable_or_distinctive: Mostly standard essay-writing advice (avoid cliches, avoid resume repetition, show growth); nothing highly distinctive beyond the general framework.
reliability_notes: Straightforward, broadly accepted essay advice; no unsupported statistics; clearly framed as promotional content for Crimson's consulting services.
